title: Marine Raider Officer (I) (LtCol to Capt) PMOS, DC PP&O
raw_text:
5.     MOS 0370, Marine Raider Officer (I) (LtCol to Capt) PMOS, DC PP&O

    a. Summary. Marine Raider Officers are Marine Officers responsible for
the organization, training, planning, employment and execution of Marine
Special Operations Force (MARSOF) formations across the spectrum of the
Special Operations Core Activities of Direct Action (DA), Special
Reconnaissance (SR), Countering Weapons of Mass Destruction (CWMD),
Counterterrorism (CT), Unconventional Warfare (UW), Foreign Internal Defense
(FID), Security Force Assistance (SFA), and Counterinsurgency (COIN), in
hostile, denied, and politically sensitive environments. The Marine Raider
Officer possess a high level of maturity, experience, judgment, and the
ability to rapidly apply critical thought to the operational environment.
They are team oriented, but are trained and ready to function as individuals



                                          1-22                        Enclosure (1)
 1106                                                               NAVMC 1200.1L



and as members of an element, team, company, battalion, or group. They are
capable of operations across the entire spectrum of special operations; from
employment in isolated and austere locales with little-to-no conventional
support to operations as fully integrated units in a variety of joint task
organized configurations. They possess advanced cultural skills and are adept
at working by, with and through partner nation forces in pursuit of strategic
goals and objectives.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must be a U.S. citizen.

            (2) Must be worldwide deployable.

            (3) No courts martial convictions.

            (4) No non-judicial punishment (NJP) as an officer.

            (5) No adverse fitness reports within the last 12 months.

            (6) No incidents with drug use or possession while in service.

            (7) No derogatory record book/OMPF entries within the last 12 months.

        (8) Any administrative action jeopardy on contract will require a CG
level waiver to attend A&S and ITC.

        (9) Must obtain a Naval Special Warfare/Special Operator (NSW/SO)
physical prior to attending assessment and selection (A&S).

        (10) Must have a first class PFT and CFT. Once awarded the 0370 MOS,
Marine Raider Officers are required to maintain a current first class PFT and
CFT, unless prevented by illness or injury.

        (11) Must be a volunteer in the grade of first lieutenant or captain.
Captains cannot have more than 24 months’ time-in grade upon reporting to
MRTC to attend the Individual Training Course-Officer (ITC-O) (M03TCMK) and
MARSOF team commanders seminar.

            (12) Security requirement:

            (a) Must be TS/SCI eligible via MARSOC SSO prior to ITC-Officer
Course graduation and assignment to the operational forces.

            (b) Must have a finally adjudicated secret security clearance
based on national agency check, law enforcement and credit check (NACLC) or
T3 background investigation prior to attending ITC. An interim secret
clearance eligibility will not be accepted.

        (13) Must obtain a passing score while physically conducting the
following separate physical fitness events in A&S phase 1:

                (a) Conduct a 5-mile run in 40:00 minimum.

                (b) Conduct two repetitions of the obstacle course in 8:00
minimum.




                                          1-23                          Enclosure (1)
 1106                                                                 NAVMC 1200.1L



            (c) By the conclusion of Phase 1, conduct a 300m swim in 13:00
minimum using breaststroke or side stroke.

            (d) Conduct a 12 mile ruck march in 3:00:00 minimum. Conducted
with a 45lbs ruck, not including water with rifle in MARPAT uniform.

            (e) Conduct a water survival qualification and achieve a water
survival intermediate (WSI) qualification. Once awarded the 0370 MOS, Marine
Raider Officers are required to have a minimum WSA swim qualification or be a
current and qualified combatant diver, unless prevented by illness or injury.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) For all Marines, awarding of the 0370 PMOS requires selection at
assessment & selection (A&S). Graduation from: the ITC-Officer Course
(M03TCMK), the MARSOF Team Commanders Seminar, the Survival, Evasion,
Resistance, and Escape (SERE) Course (M03M47K), or the Joint Equivalent SERE
Level C Course (N28M5Q1, N51M5Q1). Commander U.S. Marine Forces Special
Operations Command (COMMARFORSOC) is the awarding authority of the PMOS 0370.

        (2) Upon successful completion of the Individual Training Course
(ITC) (M03K24K) and subsequent awarding of PMOS 0370, Marine Raider Officers
are authorized to wear the Marine Raider Insignia (MRI). The MRI may be
involuntarily removed in accordance with MCO 1020.35.

        (3) Upon awarding of PMOS 0370, Marine Raider Officers must have all
necessary documentation for rapid global deployment in accordance with the
Department of Defense Foreign Clearance Guide.

        (4) To maintain the 0370 MOS the Marine must not have violated any of
the criteria established by MCO 1020.35 Involuntary Removal of the Marine
Raider Insignia.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (bw), Marine Special Operations Command Training and Readiness
Manual.

       e.   Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

            (1) Special Forces Officers 55-1017.

            (2) Infantry Officers 55-1016.

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1) Ground Intelligence Officer, 0203.

            (2) Infantry Officers, 0302.

            (3) Expeditionary Ground Reconnaissance Officer, 0307.

            (4) Advisor, 0570.

            (5) Operational Advisor, 0571.

            (6) Linguist, 27XX.

            (7) Parachutist, 8023.



                                           1-24                       Enclosure (1)
 1106                                                    NAVMC 1200.1L



       (8) Combatant Diver, 8024.

       (9) Parachutist/Combatant Diver Officer, 8026.




                                    1-25                 Enclosure (1)
 1107                                                              NAVMC 1200.1L

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
